pr_title: FileLoggerProcessor write to a new file on new instance or Fields change

issue_context.title: W3CLogger should write to a new file when Fields change
issue_context.body: If the user runs an app that uses W3CLogger, then changes the set of fields they are logging and runs the app again on the same day, it will write to the same file as before, but with the new set of fields (meaning the fields logged won't correspond to the header listing what fields are in the log). It should write to a new file when the fields option changes.

review_comments: Is there any potential race between "Message one" being written and the option being updated?
Good call, I'll add a wait for the first file to be written
:/ we should fix this at some point, i.e. have an interface for the clock so we can test without actual date times.

Completely agreed. This also stops us from testing the `_fileNumber` resetting to zero when moving to the next day. This is being tracked as part of https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/33945 but it's in the backlog. I wonder if we shouldn't split that up and mark it `help-wanted`.

We almost never use string interpolation in these pre-defined log messages unless the value we're writing here will never change. In this case the options can be updated so we don't want to embed the original value in the log.

We should pass the option to `MaxFilesReached` and also remove the `Exception` param, I don't think it's needed anywhere?

`MaxFileCount` can't be set by the user, it's hard-coded to 10,000. It's the max number of files per day before we stop logging - different from `RetainedFileCountLimit`, which determines when we start rolling files & can't be greater than `MaxFileCount`.
I removed the exception but kept the line you're commenting on

> `MaxFileCount` can't be set by the user

Ah, thought that was a settable option, log changes look good now 👍
If the file name changes should the file number reset, or be rescanned for?

Yeah, I think so, that'd be a way for users to get around the 10,000 file a day limit if they wanted to. But it might be somewhat tricky - e.g. OnChange fires in the middle of execution of WriteMessagesAsync, causing the FileNumber to go back to zero. If this happens while we're scanning through some previous files to find out if they exist, it could cause us to suffix the first file with the new name with something nonzero. I'll file a follow-up issue for this one, for now I think it's fine if the numbering for the new file names pick up where the old ones left off.
Shouldn't there be another test for changing the field options while the logger is still running?
